ASTER

Space Health Research Console

Project report — simulation-first research prototype

NASA Space Apps Challenge · Malatya · Challenge: health monitoring software for astronauts · 2026-11-14

Research prototype · Simulated data · Not a medical device · Not endorsed by NASA or any agency

1. Summary

ASTER is a working, offline-capable web application that connects three measurement-interpretation questions in one evidence-linked workflow: what air was inhaled, whether the sensor coupling changed, and whether an exercise response is comparable. A local, deterministic rule engine turns valid observations into versioned events; a store-and-forward service carries case packages over a delayed, interruptible link and attaches ground replies to the exact case revision.

This release contains the complete application (12 routes, light and dark themes, 7 locales including right-to-left Arabic), a seeded simulator with 15 fault scenarios, a held-out evaluation against baselines, two optional local server processes, 95 unit/integration tests and 10 browser tests run in three browser engines — all passing — and an independent security review whose findings were fixed.

2. Problem and prior art

Spaceflight health monitoring is not an empty field: smart garments (CSA Bio-Monitor), mechanical cardiac sensing (MagIC-Space), personal CO₂ monitors and integrated data and asynchronous medical systems (NASA CHP-IDSP, xEHR) exist or are in development. ASTER does not claim to invent these categories. The narrower question is how to make a defensible interpretation when a measurement is affected by its environment, by its attachment to the body, or by another physiological process — and to say so when it cannot.

3. The product

ModuleWhat it doesWhat it refuses to claim
Breathing & ExposureDetects inhalation from a respiratory waveform, shifts the near-face CO₂ signal by the declared sampling delay, applies a first-order response correction and reports a time-weighted inhalation-phase concentration per breath.Not an inhaled dose, not end-tidal CO₂, not a diagnosis. Withheld when the sensor is too slow or the phase is uncertain.
Sensor IntegrityUses a reference excitation response, a contact-force measurement and a motion reference to accept, reject or (experimentally) compensate each 2 s window of the mechanical signal.A passed self-check is not a physiological calibration. A calibration that disagrees with the contact measurement is rejected.
Exercise & Muscle ResponseCompares MMG amplitude per repetition with reference sessions matched by exercise, load band, cadence and signal quality; shows impedance as fluid-sensitive context.No force measurement, no atrophy diagnosis, no "muscle health" score. Unmatched sessions are not compared.

Three labels stay separate everywhere: data source (simulated, recorded, hardware, mixed), measurement state (valid, suspect, invalid, stale, unavailable) and interpretation status (observation, experimental estimate, research guidance). In the combined scenario a loosened garment makes the muscle interpretation unavailable while the independently valid exposure event stays open.

4. Architecture

TypeScript throughout. contracts (zod schemas) → engine (quality, features, estimates, rule state machines; imports contracts only) ← runtime → simulator (seeded latent scenario → noisy observation model) and comms (durable outbox, link simulator, ground station logic). evaluation joins engine output with hidden truth after the run and is never imported by the engine or the operator UI — enforced by a lint rule and a unit test. The same runtime runs in a browser Web Worker (IndexedDB) and in a local Node gateway (SQLite) that exchanges packages with a separate ground process over real HTTP. Because simulation and communication share one virtual clock, a run is fully recoverable from its seed and command log.

5. Evaluation on held-out simulation

Methods and rules were frozen, then evaluated on 20 held-out seeds per scenario (240 runs) with varied sensor dynamics the estimator does not model. The reference is simulator truth held outside the engine. These figures describe method behaviour in simulation only — not clinical sensitivity.

Local mean over whole breath (baseline)1259 ± 5831257100 %
Phase-gated, no delay compensation (baseline)1250 ± 3951250100 %
Aligned, quality-aware (candidate)284 ± 175153100 %

n = 5572 breaths; scenarios SIM-01, 02, 03, 11. The candidate had the lowest error in 70 % of runs. Exposure event missed when the reference was elevated: 0 %; raised when it was not: 0 %. With a slow sensor (SIM-04) the estimate was withheld for 100 % of breaths, where a baseline that answers anyway is off by about 1817 ppm.

Integrity — coupling fault, source unchanged (SIM-05)Feature errorCoverageLooks like a change
Fixed filter (baseline)0.585100 %100 %
Paired reference (baseline)0.655100 %100 %
Calibration-aware gate (released)—0 %—
Gate + gain compensation (experimental)0.29986 %73 %

Contact event raised 5100 ms after the slip began on average (includes a 3 s ramp and 3 s dwell), missed in 0 %; false exercise-deviation events during the fault with the released gate: 0 %; calibration-path mismatch rejected in 100 % of runs.

Exercise. With a real response change (SIM-08) the matched method flagged 99 % of samples; with a load mismatch (SIM-09) it abstained in 100 % while the unconditioned baseline wrongly flagged 54 %; during a contact fault (SIM-05) it abstained, while the ablation without the integrity gate flagged 100 %.

Negative results we keep
  • The gate is accurate by rejecting data (coverage 0 % during the fault). Gain compensation recovers coverage but leaves a systematic error (0.299) when the actuator and physiological paths scale differently, so it is shown as experimental and never feeds the exercise comparison.
  • Paired-reference cancellation did not improve on a fixed filter during coupling faults.
  • A fluid shift alone (SIM-10) still opened a false deviation event in 10 % of runs; the fluid-aware variant did not fix this and is not used by the released rule.
  • An estimator-driven sampling lag performed worse than the declared delay and was dropped; residual exposure bias is dominated by spatial sampling mismatch that software cannot remove.

6. Testing and verification

AreaVerified behaviour
Unit / integration (95 tests, 4 files)Input quarantine (unit mismatch, duplicates, out-of-order, oversized batches), staleness, all 15 scenarios' key behaviours, dwell and monotonic revisions, SHA-256 vectors, link latency lower bound, outage persistence, deduplication, stale and cross-run replies, deterministic replay, fork semantics, IndexedDB recovery, storage failure, server hardening, locale parity.
Browser end-to-end (10 tests × Chrome, Firefox, WebKit)Two-action demo start; three-module case; ground round trip with outage, duplicate and revision-linked reply; stale reply; reload and full use with the network blocked; storage-failure banner and recovery; fault injection, read-only history and fork; theme/locale persistence, RTL, keyboard reachability; automated WCAG 2.x AA checks on all 11 routes in both themes; CSP and no cross-origin requests.
Operations and performanceSIM-12 seed 7: case survived a 100 s outage, 2 duplicate deliveries ignored, 3118 B per package. 4 crew, 30 simulated minutes, SIM-01 seed 5: 3978 ms (452× real time), longest tick 9.4 ms, heap growth 44.4 MB at 30 min.

Not verified: Safari on macOS/iOS (only Playwright's WebKit build was run; keyboard link traversal was asserted in Chrome and Firefox only), any physical sensor, real-flight or human data, and long-duration field use.

7. Security review

An independent adversarial review covered the web app, the protocol layer, both servers and the supply chain. It found no critical or high-severity issue, no XSS sink, no SQL injection, no authentication bypass and no committed secret. It confirmed four medium and six low findings, mostly denial-of-service paths reachable from a local process, plus one reply-binding logic gap. All were fixed and each has a regression test.

SeverityFindingFix
MediumQuadratic regular expression in CSV number parsing (import could freeze the tab or the gateway)Field and line length caps, unambiguous pattern, regression test
MediumUnbounded package and rejection stores on the ground serverTotal and per-run caps, 256 KB body limit, summary-only listing, ring buffer
MediumUnbounded ground replies flowing into the mission runtime20 replies per package, 500 per run, persisted cursor
MediumA reply was not bound to its package's event and revision (stale flag could be defeated)Reply must match the package's event id and revision; otherwise rejected
LowNo-op commands grew the durable log; no HTTP rate limitNo-op detection, 30 requests/min per address
LowStored commands replayed without validation after recoverySchema validation of every stored row; invalid rows dropped and counted
LowAny loopback web origin was trusted by defaultDefault allow-list limited to the ASTER web origins
LowSender-chosen data-origin label on the WebSocket pathOrigin stamped at the trust boundary; sender value kept only as "claimed"
LowResponse-size, serial-parser CPU, idle WebSocket and token-over-HTTP weaknessesStreaming size cap, linear resync, idle timeout, start-up refusal

Built-in controls: strict Content-Security-Policy (no inline or remote script), no HTML injection sinks (lint-enforced), schema validation at every boundary with size limits, loopback binding by default with mandatory bearer token and Host/Origin allow-lists otherwise, parameterised SQL, no analytics or remote assets, pseudonymised case packages. Residual, documented risks: no TLS in the local servers (use a terminating proxy), the content hash is integrity not authentication, browser storage is unencrypted (synthetic data only), and one low-severity advisory in a build-time dependency has no published fix.

8. Limitations and claims

  • All physiological signals are synthetic; simulator constants are engineering assumptions, not a validated digital twin.
  • Rule thresholds are demonstration settings with no clinical meaning. Guidance cards are illustrative, non-validated workflows.
  • Integrations (replay, WebSocket, serial frame) are emulator-verified only. Bluetooth is not implemented. No hardware has been built or connected.
  • In the browser profile, closing the tab stops acquisition and analysis; this is not background medical monitoring.
  • Not claimed: clinical validation, flight readiness, NASA approval, patentability, real astronaut telemetry, reduced propagation delay.

10. Next evidence steps

Software and simulation verification (this release) → reference-instrument comparison of the exposure estimate → a controlled human study of contact gating and matched exercise comparison → an analogue environment → flight evaluation. The three main risks are near-face sampling mismatch, calibration transfer mismatch and confounded muscle-response interpretation.
